newsitem.title: RWANDA: Zaire rebels claim capture of refugee camp, town.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels claim capture of refugee camp, town.

text.p: Zairean rebels said on Sunday their forces had captured the strategic town of Lubutu and the camp where around 170,000 Hutu refugees had sheltered.
"Our forces took Tingi Tingi and Lubutu on Saturday. They are continuing to advance towards Kisangani," Mwenze Kongolo, justice minister in the rebels' administration, told Reuters by telephone.
There was no independent confirmation of the advance and no word on the fate of the refugees.
Lubutu 200 km (125 miles), southeast of Zaire's third city Kisangani, is the last town on the road from Bukavu and boasts an airstrip. The rebels have identified Kisangani as a target.
Tens of thousands of refugees started leaving Tingi Tingi on Friday fleeing the advancing rebels, according to aid workers evacuated from Kisangani on Saturday.

An estimated 170,000 Rwandan and Burundian refugees set up a makeshift camp at Tingi Tingi, beside Lubutu, after fleeing camps further to the east. Doctors said up to 40 refugees a day were dying of hunger and disease.
